tagline: Named bends above a river put to work.
intro: At Deals Gap, 1,988 feet up on the state line, US 129 crosses from North Carolina into Tennessee and takes to the forest in a run of sharp bends. It has been known as the Tail of the Dragon since 1981, and some curves carry names of their own, Copperhead Corner and Gravity Cavity among them.

Part of the road is the boundary of Great Smoky Mountains National Park, so nothing is built along it beyond a few overlooks and pull-offs. Down in the valley, Alcoa dammed the Little Tennessee River to power its aluminum smelting in Blount County.

moments.title: Deals Gap
moments.text: Motorcycle and sports car drivers cross the pass here into Tennessee, where the Dragon is said to fit 318 curves into 11 miles.

moments.title: Calderwood Overlook
moments.text: Just south of Housley Road, an overlook on US 129 looks over the Calderwood Reservoir, and a gravel road open only on foot leads from it to the 1930 dam.

moments.title: Calderwood
moments.text: Down Housley Road, gated at night, a 1950 school and a Quonset-hut theater outlast the dam crews' houses, of which only foundations and two garages remain.
